To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed a panel of analytical methods for unambiguous identification of 16 non-steroidal drugs in raw milk.

a multi-residue reversed phase LC/ESI-ITMS/MS method was developed for the identification and confirmation of salicylic acid (SAL), naproxen (NAP), carprofen (CAR), flurbiprofen (FLB), ibuprofen (IBU), meclofenamic (MFA), niflumic (NIF) acids, flunixin (FLU) and its metabolite (5-OHFLU) in milk, and

we developed a panel of multi-residue LC/ESI-IT-MS/MS methods to unambiguously confirm 15 NSAIDs in milk, which were representative of different subclasses not chemically related, with the only exception of salicylic acid.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a multi-residue analytical procedure that allows the identification of sixteen NSAIDs in raw milk.
the development of a panel of multi-residue methods for the identification of NSAIDs in milk.
the development of a panel of methods that can be used in the confirmation of NSAIDs detected at the concentration of 5 microg/ kg in raw milk.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the methods are fully in compliance with the requirements of the Decision 2002-657/EC.
the developed methods are suitable for the confirmation of the presence in raw milk of the NSAIDs under investigation.
the methods developed are reliable and can be applied for routine analysis of the NSAIDs investigated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the methods developed for the confirmation of NSAIDs residues in raw milk are reliable, sensitive, rapid and cost-effective.
the proposed methods are suitable to identify the target drugs in raw milk at 5 micro g/kg, in accordance with Decision 2002 /657/EC.
the methods are suitable to confirm the presence of the sixteen NSAIDs in raw milk, and that they can be successfully used for the identification of the drugs in other matrices.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed methods can be successfully used for confirmatory purposes of the presence of the sixteen NSAIDs in milk.
, for all drugs, the MS/MS spectra were characteristic and allowed unequivocal identification.
, by means of the LC-MS/MS techniques described herein, all the NSAIDs considered were identified and/or confirmed in the concentration range of 0.5-5.0 microg/kg.
